reference.title: The screens of the app
reference.shortdesc: What each place in the list on the left shows, with a picture of each screen.

section.title: The list on the left
section.p: A list of five places runs down the left side of every screen, whichever way up you hold the iPad. The place you are in is shaded. The first four are the main places. Some show your whole tree. Others show one person, the person named in the chip that starts with . The chip shows once you open someone.

table.title: The main places and what they show

row.entry: Your family trees, one card for each.
A drawing of the person with parents, partners and children.
The things that happened in that person's life.

section.p: The search box and the button are along the top of every screen. Above them, a line names the tree and the page you are on. Choose a name in that line to go back to that page. A back arrow at the top left takes you back one screen.
section.note: If a page says Select a person or shows only the search box, it needs a person first. Search for someone, then open them. shows how.

section.p: This is the first screen. Each card is one family tree. It tells you how many people, families and events the tree holds. starts here.
This is one person's page: their names, their birth and death, their family and their photos. shows how to open it.

section.title: When the iPad is upright
section.p: The pictures in this manual show the iPad on its side. Upright, the screen is narrower, and some screens change.

ul.li: The list on the left stays.
A person's page and the forms are in one column. is further down, so scroll to find it.
Search results are in one column, people above events. Buttons above them show everything, only the people or only the events.
The cards on are one under another.
